item.title: Why I Can't Stick To One Web Browser
item.description: Because they all suck. I think Opera is my favorite browser. I’ve been using it for many years, it’s fast, cross-platform, it was the first browser to support tabs, [speed dial](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Features_of_the_Opera_ web_browser#Speed_Dial) (with keyboard shortcuts – very useful!), and it’s always easy to block an arbitrary item of a website with Opera. However, among all the browser I’ve been using, Opera had problems with the biggest number of websites. Be it banks, Google Picasaweb, or some other sites – I can’t use Opera as my only browser.

I’ve already mentioned my linux-related laptop problems [some time ago](/2009/11/09/how-ive-stopped-being-a-desktop- linux-enthusiast/). Some things changed since then. Canonical released a new version of Ubuntu, 10.04, which in my opinion is a huge improvement over 9.10, and I got a new laptop (kindly provided by HiB), an [HP EliteBook 6930p](http://h10010.www1.hp.com/wwpc/no/no/sm/WF25a/321957-321957-6 4295-3955549-3955549-3688868.html). Old problems are gone, but new have arisen. At first it all seemed ok. I’ve installed Ubuntu 10.04 and didn’t have to tweak anything.

item.title: How I stopped being a desktop linux enthusiast
item.description: It’s actually about “how I’m stopping to be a desktop linux enthusiast”, because I’m still using linux on my desktop/laptop, and I still think it’s a much better solution than any Windows OS. It’s just that I’ve been using various linux distributions for many many years (since 1998 I guess) on every computer I’ve owned and thought it is a nearly flawless system. It’s not, and in fact it’s getting on my nerves.
